'''Linda Hong Zhao''' is a Chinese-American [[statistician]]. She is a Professor of Statistics and at the [[Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania]]. She is a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]. Zhao specializes in modern [[machine learning]] methods.

== Early life and education ==
In 1982, Zhao obtained her [[Bachelor of Science]] from the Department of Mathematics at [[Nankai University]]. She later emigrated to the United States and attended [[Cornell University]], where she obtained her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D]] from the Department of Statistics in 1993.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Biography of Linda H. Zhao|url=http://www.whartonbeijing09.com/bio-zhao.html|access-date=2020-06-09|website=www.whartonbeijing09.com}}</ref>

== Career ==
Zhao became an assistant professor statistics at [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 1993,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Linda Zhao|url=https://statistics.wharton.upenn.edu/profile/lzhao/|access-date=2020-06-09|website=Statistics Department|language=en-US}}</ref> before joining the [[Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania|Wharton School]] in 1994, where she is currently a Professor of Statistics.<ref>{{Citation|last1=George|first1=Edward I.|title=Strength in Numbers: The Rising of Academic Statistics Departments in the U. S.|date=2012|chapter-url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-1-4614-3649-2_34|page=474|editor-last=Agresti|editor-first=Alan|chapter=University of Pennsylvania Department of Statistics|place=New York, NY|publisher=Springer|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-1-4614-3649-2_34|last2=Krieger|first2=Abba M.|last3=Morrison|first3=Donald F.|last4=Shaman|first4=Paul|isbn=978-1-4614-3648-5 |editor2-last=Meng|editor2-first=Xiao-Li}}</ref>

Her specialty falls in modern [[machine learning]] methods, replicability in science, high dimensional data, housing price prediction, and [[Bayesian statistics|Bayesian]] methods.<ref name=":0" /> Current projects include equity ownership network, and its relationship to firm performance and innovation activities; identify signals from noisy data using non-parametric Bayesian scheme; and model-free data analysis.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Welcome to Linda Zhao's homepage !|url=http://www-stat.wharton.upenn.edu/~lzhao/|access-date=2020-06-09|website=www-stat.wharton.upenn.edu}}</ref> Her work has won [[National Science Foundation]] support for over 20 years.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NSF Award Search: Award#1512084 - Valid Inference when Analytical Models are Approximations|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1512084|access-date=2020-06-09|website=www.nsf.gov}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Zhao was married to [[Lawrence D. Brown]] (1940–2018), a fellow statistician at the Wharton School.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Berger|first1=James|last2=Cai|first2=Tony|last3=Johnstone|first3=Iain|date=2018-05-15|title=Obituary: Lawrence Brown, 1940–2018|url=https://imstat.org/2018/05/15/obituary-lawrence-brown-1940-2018/|access-date=2020-06-10|website=Institute of Mathematical Statistics|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brown|first1=Larry|last2=DasGupta|first2=Anirban|date=2005|title=A Conversation with Larry Brown|url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/20061170|journal=Statistical Science|volume=20|issue=2|page=199|jstor=20061170 |issn=0883-4237}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
* Fellow, [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], 2017<ref>{{Cite web|title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics {{!}} 2017 IMS Fellows|url=https://imstat.org/2017/06/05/2017-ims-fellows/|access-date=2020-06-09|language=en}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
* Zhao, L. H. (2000) Bayesian aspects of some nonparametric problems, The [[Annals of Statistics]], 28, 532–552. [http://dx.doi.org/10.1214/aos/1016218229 doi:10.1214/aos/1016218229]
* Mao, V. and Zhao, L. H. (2003) Free knot polynomial splines with confidence intervals, Journal of the [[Royal Statistical Society]], Series B, 65, 901-919.  [[doi:10.1046/j.1369-7412.2003.00422.x]]
* Berk, R., Brown, L.B. and Zhao, L. (2010) Statistical inference after [[model selection]], Journal of Quantitative Criminology, 26, 217-236 [https://www.dx.Doi.org/10.1007/s10940-009-9077-7 doi:10.1007/s10940-009-9077-7]
* Nagaraja, C. H., Brown, L.D. and Zhao, L. (2010) An autoregressive approach to house price modeling, to appear The Annals of Applied Statistics. [https://www.dx.Doi.org/10.1214/10-AOAS380 doi:10.1214/10-AOAS380]
